```{r}
mapping_path <- "../../../Input/Harmonized_Datasets/Targeted_Analyte_Category_Mapping.csv"
targeted_mapping <- read_targeted_analyte_mapping(mapping_path)

plot_categories <- c(
  "TraceElements", "Phenols", "Phthalates", "PAH", "PCB", "Parabens",
  "Smoking", "Pesticides", "VOCs", "FlameRetardants", "PFAS"
)

targeted_category_lookup <- targeted_mapping %>%
  dplyr::filter(Category %in% plot_categories) %>%
  dplyr::select(Code, Category) %>%
  dplyr::distinct()

theme_codes <- targeted_theme_codes(targeted_mapping)

get_theme <- function(category_name) {
  if (category_name %in% names(theme_codes)) {
    unique(theme_codes[[category_name]])
  } else {
    character()
  }
}

Trace_Elements_Theme <- get_theme("TraceElements")
Phenols_Theme <- get_theme("Phenols")
PAH_Theme <- get_theme("PAH")
Phthalates_Theme <- get_theme("Phthalates")
Parabens_Theme <- get_theme("Parabens")
Smoking_Theme <- get_theme("Smoking")
Inflam_Theme <- get_theme("Inflammation")
Pesticide_Theme <- get_theme("Pesticides")
VOC_Theme <- get_theme("VOCs")
OXID_Theme <- get_theme("OxidativeStress")
PFAS_Theme <- get_theme("PFAS")
Flame_Retardant_Theme <- get_theme("FlameRetardants")
PCB_Theme <- get_theme("PCB")
Other_Theme <- character()

add_plot_category <- function(data, code_col = "Outcome") {
  dplyr::left_join(
    data,
    targeted_category_lookup,
    by = stats::setNames("Code", code_col)
  )
}
```

```{r}
    # Collapse various US-specific locations to a single "United_States"
    Location_Country = dplyr::case_when(
      Location %in% c(
        "United_States","NorthEast_US","New_Hampshire","Washington_State",
        "Midwestern_US","Denver","Baltimore","Sacramento",
        "Southern_California","Syracuse","Michigan","California",
        "SanFrancisco","Massachusetts"
      ) ~ "United_States",
      TRUE ~ "Worldwide"

    # Binary maternal education bucket
    Mat_Edu_Binary = dplyr::case_when(
      Mat_Edu %in% c("No_Education","Primary_Education","Primary_School","High_School") ~ "No_College",
      Mat_Edu %in% c("Some_College","Four_Year_College_Degree","Some_Grad_School") ~ "Some_College",
      Mat_Edu == "Not_Reported" ~ NA_character_,
      TRUE ~ NA_character_  # CHECK: any unexpected levels?

      Mat_Income %in% c("50_74k","75_99k","100_124k","Over_100k","Over_125k","Over_49k") ~ "Over_49k",

    )
  )
```

Results Parse Function
-----
```{r}
Parse_Results <- function(Results_List = Child_SDOH_Metab_Quantile_Results_SexByStudy,Cohort_Meta = Cohort_Meta){
  
  
  if(Cohort_Meta == T){
    
    All_Res <- list()
  
  for(i in seq_along(Results_List)){
    
    curr_study <- Results_List[[i]]
    
             #print(i)
      
         curr_results <- try(curr_study[[1]][["Regression_Results"]] %>% 
             dplyr::filter(Variable != "(Intercept)") %>% 
             mutate(
            Study = names(Results_List[i])) )

         if(is.character(curr_results)){
           next
         }
         
         All_Res[[i]] <- curr_results
        
  }
  Final_Res <- bind_rows(All_Res)
    
  }else{
  
  
  All_Res <- list()
  
  for(i in seq_along(Results_List)){
    
    curr_study <- Results_List[[i]]
    
    curr_study_all_res <- list() 
             #print(i)

    for(j in seq_along(curr_study)){
      
         curr_results <- try(curr_study[[j]][[1]][["Regression_Results"]] %>% 
             dplyr::filter(Variable != "(Intercept)") %>% 
             mutate(
            Study = names(Results_List[i])) )

         if(is.character(curr_results)){
           next
         }
         
         curr_study_all_res[[j]] <- curr_results
        
      }
      
      curr_study_all_res <-  curr_study_all_res[lengths(curr_study_all_res) != 0]

    Results <- bind_rows(curr_study_all_res)
    
      All_Res[[i]] <- Results

  }
  Final_Res <- bind_rows(All_Res)
  }
# FDR SCOPE (fixed 2026-08-11, CODE_AUDIT_2026-08-11.md section 2.8).
# p.adjust() used to run INSIDE the loop above, correcting across the handful of
# coefficients in a single model rather than across the whole scan. It now runs
# once, on the bound results, via apply_scan_fdr() in harmonization_helpers.R.
# That helper also asserts the p-values are not all NA, which is what happens
# when the upstream fit was run with summary_R < 25 (see audit section 1.5).
  return(apply_scan_fdr(Final_Res, what = "Within_Study_SDOH_Compare / Final_Res"))
}
```


Process Results
----------

```{r}
Process_Quant_Results <- function(Mat_Quant_Results) {
  All_Outcome_Results_Mat <- list()
  
  for (i in seq_along(Mat_Quant_Results)) {
    Curr_Reg_Results <- Mat_Quant_Results[[i]]
    Curr_Reg_Results <- Filter(is.list, Curr_Reg_Results)
    
    All_Reg_Results <- list()
    for (j in seq_along(Curr_Reg_Results)) {
      Res <- Curr_Reg_Results[[j]][[1]]
      All_Reg_Results[[j]] <- Res
    }
    
    if (length(All_Reg_Results) == 0) {
      next
    }
    
    All_Reg_Results <- bind_rows(All_Reg_Results) %>%
      filter(!str_detect(Variable, "(Intercept)"))
    
    All_Outcome_Results_Mat[[i]] <- All_Reg_Results
    names(All_Outcome_Results_Mat)[i] <- unique(All_Reg_Results$Outcome)
  }
  
  All_Outcome_Results_Mat_Df <- bind_rows(All_Outcome_Results_Mat)
# FDR SCOPE (fixed 2026-08-11, CODE_AUDIT_2026-08-11.md section 2.8).
# p.adjust() used to run INSIDE the loop above, correcting across the handful of
# coefficients in a single model rather than across the whole scan. It now runs
# once, on the bound results, via apply_scan_fdr() in harmonization_helpers.R.
# That helper also asserts the p-values are not all NA, which is what happens
# when the upstream fit was run with summary_R < 25 (see audit section 1.5).
  return(apply_scan_fdr(All_Outcome_Results_Mat_Df, what = "Within_Study_SDOH_Compare / All_Outcome_Results_Mat_Df"))
}

```

```{r}
make_results_bystudy <- function(results_list,Model_Type,Population) {
  all_results <- lapply(seq_along(results_list), function(i) {
    curr_study <- names(results_list)[i]
    Process_Quant_Results(Mat_Quant_Results = results_list[[i]]) %>%
      mutate(
        Model_Type = Model_Type,
        Study = curr_study,
        Population = Population
      )
  })
  
  bind_rows(all_results)
}

```

```{r}

ALl_R2 <-All_R2_Data %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(Model_Type = ifelse(Model_Type == "All_SDOH","Additional_Socio_Values",Model_Type))

unique(ALl_R2$Model_Type)
model_seq <- unique(ALl_R2$Model_Type)
element_lengths <- nchar(model_seq)

sorted_indices <- order(element_lengths)

# Sort the original vector using these indices
model_seq <- model_seq[sorted_indices]

df_f <- ALl_R2 %>% 
  #group_by(Outcome,Tau,Population,Model_Type,Category,pseudo_R) %>% 
  #summarise(All_Vars = paste(unique(Demo_Var), collapse = ":")) %>% 
  #mutate(plot_R2 = ifelse(pseudo_R <= 0,0,pseudo_R)) %>% 
  #dplyr::filter(Tau == 0.50) %>%  
  filter(Model_Type %in% model_seq) %>% 
  group_by(Study, Model_Type) %>% 
  #dplyr::filter(Study == "CCREOH") %>% 
  summarise(mean_R2 = mean(plot_R2, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%  
  arrange(Study, match(Model_Type, model_seq)) %>%
  group_by(Study) %>%
  mutate(
    # Force baseline to 0 and ensure monotonic increase
    #mean_R2 = cummax(mean_R2),  
    total_R2 = max(mean_R2, na.rm = TRUE),
    contrib = pmax(mean_R2 - lag(mean_R2, default = 0), 0),
    component = if_else(row_number() == 1,
                        paste0("Baseline: ", Model_Type),
                        paste0("+ ", Model_Type))
  ) %>%
  ungroup() 

comp_levels <- model_seq

pool <- c(
  "#FED439FF", "#709AE1FF", "#8A9197FF", "#D2AF81FF",
  "#FD7446FF", "#D5E4A2FF", "#197EC0FF", "#F05C3BFF",
  "#46732EFF", "#71D0F5FF", "#370335FF", "#075149FF",
  "#C80813FF", "#91331FFF", "#1A9993FF", "#FD8CC1FF"
)
mypal <- setNames(pool[seq_along(comp_levels)], comp_levels)

df_plot <- df_f%>%
  mutate(
    Study  = fct_reorder(Study, total_R2),
    component = factor(Model_Type, levels = comp_levels)
  ) %>% 
  group_by(Study) %>%
  arrange(Study, component, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  # compute stack geometry
  mutate(
    xmin = cumsum(lag(contrib, default = 0)),
    xmax = xmin + contrib,
    xmid = (xmin + xmax) / 2,
    frac = contrib / sum(contrib, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  # flag largest slice (break ties deterministically by first factor level)
  mutate(is_max = contrib == max(contrib, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(component = factor(component, levels = names(mypal)))

totals <- df_plot %>%
  group_by(Study) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(contrib, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

fill_order <- rev(c(
  "SY","Age", "Age_Sex","Age_Edu","Age_Race","Age_Sex_Edu","Age_Sex_Race","Age_Race_Edu",
  "Age_Sex_Race_Edu","Additional_Socio_Values"
))


df_plot2 <- df_plot %>% 
  group_by(Study) %>% 
  mutate(
    total_R2_study = max(total_R2, na.rm = TRUE),        # the max you want bar to reach
    prop_of_total  = contrib / sum(contrib, na.rm = TRUE),# share of contribution
    contrib_scaled = prop_of_total * total_R2_study       # rescaled so bar = total_R2
  ) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  dplyr::filter(Study != "DISCOVER") 

df_plot2$Model_Type <- factor(df_plot2$Model_Type, levels = fill_order)




pdf(file = "../../../Output/Paper1_Output_Submission2/Plots/R2_Barplot_ByStudy.pdf",height=10,width = 10)
r2_barplot <- ggplot(df_plot2, aes(x = contrib_scaled, y = Study, fill = Model_Type)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = mypal, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.06)),
    labels = label_number(accuracy = 0.01)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Demographic Contribution by Model",
    x = expression(Contribution~to~prediction~("(" * mean~R^2 * ")")),
    y = "",
    fill = "Model term"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title      = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    axis.title.x    = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y    = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x     = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y     = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.4),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y    = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title    = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    legend.text     = element_text(size = 10)
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, max(df_plot2$total_R2_study, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.12))

r2_barplot_bystudy <- r2_barplot
print(r2_barplot_bystudy)
```

```{r}
Plot_Targeted <- Targeted_Data_All %>%                          # keep child samples
  mutate(
    Units = if_else(is.na(Units), "ng/mL", Units),        # default units
    Concentration = to_ng_per_mL(Concentration, Units)    # normalize units
  ) %>%
      mutate(Study = std_study(Study)) %>%                   # standardize label
  mutate(Sample_Collection_Year = as.numeric(Sample_Collection_Year)) %>%
```

```{r}
plot_sum <- Plot_Targeted %>%
  group_by(Study, Sample_Collection_Year, Category) %>%
  summarise(
    n      = n(),
    median = median(Concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    q25    = quantile(Concentration, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75    = quantile(Concentration, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(str_detect(Study,paste0(over_5,collapse = "|")))


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## IMHRD supplementary panel (added 2026-08)
##
## IMHRD cannot enter Harmonized_Targeted -- it ships ONLY aggregated year x
## analyte statistics (median / IQR / LOQ / n) with no participant records, so
## there is no per-person value to pool. It is however the most year-rich of the
## new cohorts: 21 collection years (2003-2023), comfortably past the >=5-year
## threshold above, where GRAPHS has only 3.
##
## To show it without inventing a data path, we feed the reconstruction built by
## Coding/IMHRD_Reconstruct_Distribution.R (a deterministic lognormal quantile
## lattice matched to each cell's published median + IQR) through the SAME
## unit-normalisation / category / group_by-summarise code used for every other
## study, so the panel is computed identically rather than special-cased.
##
## The facet is labelled "IMHRD (reconstructed)" so it can never be mistaken for
## participant-level data. Marginals only -- do not read it as individual-level.
## If the reconstruction is absent the block is skipped and the figure is
## unchanged, so this Rmd still knits standalone.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
imhrd_recon <- "../../../Input/Reference/IMHRD_PFAS_Reconstructed.RData"
if (file.exists(imhrd_recon)) {
  imhrd_env <- new.env(); load(imhrd_recon, envir = imhrd_env)
  imhrd_sum <- imhrd_env$IMHRD_Reconstructed %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Units = dplyr::if_else(is.na(Units), "ng/mL", Units),
      Concentration = to_ng_per_mL(Concentration, Units),
      Sample_Collection_Year = as.numeric(Sample_Collection_Year)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(Sample_Collection_Year >= 1980) %>%
    add_plot_category(code_col = "Analyte_Code") %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(Category)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Study = "IMHRD (reconstructed)") %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Study, Sample_Collection_Year, Category) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      n      = dplyr::n(),
      median = median(Concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
      q25    = quantile(Concentration, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
      q75    = quantile(Concentration, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  message("IMHRD supplementary panel: ", nrow(imhrd_sum), " year x category rows, ",
          dplyr::n_distinct(imhrd_sum$Sample_Collection_Year), " collection years")
  plot_sum <- dplyr::bind_rows(plot_sum, imhrd_sum)
} else {
  message("IMHRD reconstruction not found - secular-time panel built without it. ",
          "Run Coding/IMHRD_Reconstruct_Distribution.R to include it.")
}


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Presentation fixes (2026-08):
##
##  1. EQUAL-DECADE y axes. Three options were on the table and the middle one
##     wins:
##       - fully free y (the original): each panel autoscales, so a study whose
##         medians sit at 0.02 ng/mL and one at 63 draw identical flat lines.
##         A given vertical distance means a different fold-change in every
##         panel, so no trend can be compared against any other.
##       - fully shared y: honest about magnitude, but the pooled range is 4.76
##         decades while the median study needs only 1.96. Most panels ended up
##         near-empty with their trends flattened into horizontal lines --
##         worse than the problem it solved.
##       - equal SPAN, free POSITION (this): every panel covers the same number
##         of decades, centred on its own data. Vertical distance now means the
##         same fold-change everywhere, so slopes ARE comparable, and each
##         panel is filled. Absolute level is read off the axis labels, which
##         differ by panel -- that trade is stated in the subtitle.
##     Span is max(3 decades, what the study needs), so nothing is ever
##     clipped; 14 of 16 studies land on exactly 3 (DCHS needs 4.14, CHARGE
##     3.39). To go back to plain autoscaling, drop the geom_blank layer below.
##  2. log10 rather than log1p. All medians and IQR bounds are strictly
##     positive (min q25 = 0.0011), and log1p is near-linear below 1, which
##     crushed the low-concentration studies. Fixed decade breaks also end the
##     tick collisions that made CEHC/CHARGE/MARBLES/SEARCH/MDUC print
##     "50/40/30/20" on top of itself.
##  3. IMHRD is drawn dashed on a lightly tinted panel. It is reconstructed
##     from published summaries, not participant data, and previously rendered
##     identically to real cohorts -- distinguishable only by the facet title.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
plot_sum <- plot_sum %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Is_Reconstructed = Study == "IMHRD (reconstructed)")

recon_panels <- plot_sum %>%
  dplyr::filter(Is_Reconstructed) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Study)

## Two invisible anchor points per study fix that panel's y range under
## scales = "free". x is set to a year the study actually has, so this cannot
## widen the x range.
MIN_DECADES <- 3
y_anchors <- plot_sum %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Study) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    lo = min(q25, na.rm = TRUE),
    hi = max(q75, na.rm = TRUE),
    x  = min(Sample_Collection_Year, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    span = pmax(MIN_DECADES, log10(hi / lo)) + 0.12,   # 0.12 = breathing room
    mid  = (log10(lo) + log10(hi)) / 2,
    ymin = 10^(mid - span / 2),
    ymax = 10^(mid + span / 2)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Study, x, ymin, ymax) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(ymin, ymax), names_to = NULL, values_to = "y")

sum_yr <- ggplot(
  plot_sum,
  aes(
    x = Sample_Collection_Year,
    y = median,
    color = Category,
    fill  = Category,
    group = Category
  )
) +
  # tint the reconstructed panel so it reads as different in kind
  geom_rect(data = recon_panels, inherit.aes = FALSE,
            xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
            fill = "grey95") +
  # invisible anchors that equalise the decade span of every panel
  geom_blank(data = y_anchors, aes(x = x, y = y), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  # ribbons behind lines
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75),
              alpha = 0.18, linewidth = 0, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = Is_Reconstructed), linewidth = 1.05) +
  # anchor the median at each year (optional but often helps)
  geom_point(aes(size = n), alpha = 0.9) +

  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "solid", `TRUE` = "22"),
                        guide = "none") +
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Samples (n)", range = c(0.7, 3.4),
                        breaks = scales::breaks_extended(3)) +
  scale_y_log10(
    breaks = 10^(-5:3),
    labels = function(v) trimws(formatC(v, format = "fg", digits = 3)),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))
  ) +
  # n = 4, not 6: with free x, six breaks pushed the last label of one panel
  # into the first label of the next along the whole facet row.
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = pretty_breaks(n = 4),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.04, 0.04))
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(values = mypal, name = "Category") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = mypal, guide = "none") +

  facet_wrap(~Study, scales = "free") +

  labs(
    title = "Median Concentration Over Time - Studies with five or more sample collection years",
    subtitle = paste("Lines show yearly medians; ribbons show IQR (25th-75th percentile); point size shows sample size.",
                     "\nEvery panel spans the same number of log decades, so the STEEPNESS of a trend is comparable across studies;",
                     "absolute level is not - read it off each panel's own axis.",
                     "\nDashed line on the tinted panel: IMHRD, reconstructed from published year-level summary statistics (no participant-level data)."),
    x = "Sample collection year",
    y = "Median concentration, ng/mL (log10 scale)"
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18, hjust = 0),
    #plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, color = "grey30", margin = margin(b = 8)),

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.4),

    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = NA),
    strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),

    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text  = element_text(color = "grey15"),

    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.text  = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.key.height = unit(0.35, "cm"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, color = "grey30", margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 8)),
    legend.margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 6),
    panel.spacing.x = unit(1.8, "lines"),   # keeps adjacent year labels apart
    panel.spacing.y = unit(1.0, "lines")
  ) +
  guides(
    color = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE, override.aes = list(linewidth = 2))
  )



# 4 rows x 4 cols. At 15x20 each panel was ~5in wide by ~3.2in tall, so the
# series were stretched flat; taller and narrower gives roughly square panels.
pdf(file = "../../../Output/Paper1_Output_Submission2/Plots/Conc_ByYear.pdf",height=18,width = 17)
print(sum_yr)
dev.off()
save(sum_yr, file = "../../../Output/Paper1_Output_Submission2/Plots/conc_year.RData")

```

```{r}
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.4),

    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text  = element_text(color = "grey20"),

    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.text  = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.key.height = unit(0.35, "cm"),
    legend.margin =  ggplot2::margin(t = 6),

    panel.spacing = unit(0.8, "lines")
  ) +
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)
  )
save(year_hist, file = "../../../Output/Paper1_Output_Submission2/Plots/year_hist.RData")
```
